header: r18.L6 · The test architect who has seen coverage lie · sonnet
verdict: The round-17 write pass resolves all seven of my findings as stated, but it leaves two behavior gaps in the RJ-338 mechanism (the changed path cannot be named from a stored sha256, and a failed fresh-fingerprint read has no row) and one contradiction between the 04 4.1 hint shape and the byte-asserted RJ-338 hint.

prior_resolution_notes.L6-r17-1: resolved as stated (R17-01, T): T068 acceptance holds 'write during the salvage' with the precondition and a writer that outlasts the repeat
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r17-2: resolved as stated (R17-02, T): T068 holds the --accept-loss=worktree-changing case; I17 still says 'naming any reason', accepted as test-detail
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r17-3: resolved as stated (R17-08, T): T068 asserts RJ-338/RJ-306 for rm and recreate, T069 for retire
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r17-4: resolved as stated (R17-09): kill point set in T068; 01 1.6 says the state decides, with no marker; RJ-338 says 'killed'
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r17-5: resolved as stated (R17-04): J3 step 5 and the rm row cite 04 4.4 and the newest fingerprint
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r17-6: resolved as stated (R17-06): hint amended and T008 holds a byte test; the hint's shape against 04 4.1 is a new finding (L6-r18-3)
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r17-7: resolved as stated (R17-10): 'byte order' and 'greatest salvage id' added; both rest on gaps reported as L6-r18-1 and L6-r18-4

findings.defect: RJ-338 details are to name the first path whose entry changed, but the state stores only a plain sha256 of the fingerprint values and no other store keeps the old per-entry values (daemon heads and HEADs are not paths at all).
findings.scenario: T068 and I17 assert that the details name the changed path; an implementer cannot compute it from a hash, so the test goes red, or an unspecified entries file is invented, or the assertion is weakened.
findings.change: Either store the sorted entry digests beside the fingerprint (a field of the 3.8 entry or a file in the salvage dir) or say the details name the kind of entry that differs; cost: one field or one clause.
findings.evidence: 03-formats.md:482 'the plain sha256 (3.12) of the values ... whose details name the first path, in byte order, whose entry changed'; 04-cli.md:326 'The details name the first path, in byte order, whose entry changed'

findings.defect: The two present-sandbox rows of `removing` assume the fresh fingerprint can always be read, but it reads the daemon heads and worktree status inside the sandbox, and no row, exit code or state covers a stopped or unreachable sandbox or a failed read.
findings.scenario: After a failed sbx env rm the sandbox is stopped; the rerun cannot read the fingerprint; the implementation picks an exit and leaves the generation stuck in removing, where every other mutating command exits 2 with removal-pending.
findings.change: One clause: a fingerprint that cannot be read counts as differing (the salvage then runs and its own failure rows apply), plus one I17 case; cost: a clause and a case.
findings.evidence: 01-system-model.md:312-313 'finds the sandbox present, and a fresh fingerprint ... equals / differs from the newest `fingerprint` written with `removing`'

findings.defect: 4.1 says a fix hint begins with a command line or `decide:`, but the RJ-338 hint, fixed byte for byte by T008, begins with prose and names no command line.
findings.scenario: A contributor who enforces the 4.1 shape breaks the T008 golden, and one who keeps the golden breaks 4.1.
findings.change: Loosen 4.1 to allow a prose hint that names the next step, or begin the RJ-338 hint with its command (operator-decided text); cost: one clause. Medium confidence, since other quoted hints are prose too.
findings.evidence: 04-cli.md:14 'A fix hint begins with a command line the user can run ... or with `decide:` and the choice'; 04-cli.md:326 'The hint is one fixed text: "If nothing writes in the sandbox any more, rerun; ..."'

findings.defect: 'The newest is the entry with the greatest salvage id' assumes an ordered id, but no page says a salvage id is a ULID (only the example looks like one), and a host clock stepping back would reorder it.
findings.scenario: Two salvage ids compare against the order they were written; the rerun compares with the wrong fingerprint.
findings.change: Say the newest is the last entry of `salvage[]`; cost: one sentence.
findings.evidence: 03-formats.md:482 'the newest is the entry with the greatest salvage id'; 03-formats.md:466 example id '01j9zd0a...'

findings.defect: The `salvaging` restart row says the earlier command was 'killed, or failed', but a failed sandbox half goes to `open` by the next row, so 'failed' cannot leave `salvaging`.
findings.scenario: The generated every-row test must build a state the table says cannot occur.
findings.evidence: 01-system-model.md:303 'the earlier command was killed, or failed' and :304 'the sandbox half fails ... | open'

findings.defect: Line 343 says `salvaging` with no record is 'resumed by the next salvage, which verifies the refs already created', while row 303 and the new paragraph say the next salvage restarts under a new salvage id.
findings.scenario: A reader cannot tell whether the old refs are verified or abandoned; the fault-injection test converges either way.
findings.change: Say a new salvage id is minted and the earlier refs are left; cost: one sentence.
findings.evidence: 01-system-model.md:343-346 'is resumed by the next salvage, which verifies the refs already created' vs :303 'new salvage id'

findings.defect: The --accept-loss test of RJ-338 accepts a skipped worktree-changing, but the fingerprint is 'the values step 2 and verification read' and it is undefined which read a skipped worktree contributes, so the test cannot assert what the next rerun does.
findings.scenario: Two builds record different values; both are safe (a wrong guess only salvages again) but a test cannot tell which is right.
findings.change: State the value (the last capture) in the T068 acceptance item; cost: a clause.
findings.evidence: plan.md T068 'the new entry records the accepted reason, and `sbx env rm` is not reached'; 03-formats.md:482 'the values that step 2 ... read, not read again at that write'

findings.defect: The hint's second route (edit `salvage.excludeIgnored`, then rerun) goes through `romeu sync`, which promotes and then exits 2 with removal-pending; the hint does not say that exit is expected.
findings.scenario: A user sees exit 2 after the sync and thinks the edit failed.
findings.change: Add 'romeu sync exits 2 with removal-pending after it promotes' to the decided hint, a change that needs the operator; cost: one clause.
findings.evidence: 04-cli.md:326 'for an ignored path, add it to `salvage.excludeIgnored` (gate 2); then rerun'; round-17.md R17-12 'whether the hint says so is part of R17-06'

findings.defect: parked for B: the test that parses every command line in a fix hint and in a --help example has no task in the plan, so removing that guard turns nothing named red.
findings.scenario: A hint names a flag the command lacks and CI stays green.
findings.change: Give the test an acceptance item in T008 or the generator task; cost: one bullet.
findings.evidence: 04-cli.md:14 'a test over the generated command definitions parses every command line in a fix hint and in a `--help` example'; plan.md T008 lists no such test

what_is_missing: Where and when the fresh fingerprint is read and what a failed read does; where the old per-entry values live; a defined order for 'newest'; the value a skipped worktree adds to the fingerprint; signal behavior (killed against interrupted exec) for Ctrl-C during a salvage; a plan task for the hint command-line test.

postmortem: The product fails after v1.0.0 because benign background writers keep RJ-338 firing and --accept-loss cannot end it, so users remove the sandbox by hand; the details cannot name a path from a hash; a failed fingerprint read strands a removing generation; one interrupted romeu skips the guard with a window that has no reopening trigger; and the hint contradicts 4.1 and is frozen by a byte test. Sections: 01 1.6, 03 3.8, 04 4.1 and 4.4, I17.
lens_critique: This lens measures success by named red tests, which is right for guards but blind to behaviors a spec promises that no stored data can support; a test can be named and still unsatisfiable (L6-r18-1).
missing_viewpoint: The owner of failure and degraded-mode behavior: what each command does when a read it depends on fails, as opposed to when it succeeds or differs.
out_of_scope: Token and maintainer-block rows, the 10 10.2 item g and h edits, ADR 0011, 12 12.x; the first-removal window (decided, R17-11); 05 5.4 rows.
confidence: medium-high on L6-r18-1, -4, -5, -6; medium on L6-r18-2 and L6-r18-3; the sandbox behavior behind L6-r18-2 is inferred, not tested
